title: Through the Concrete Tunnel
story:
The morning sun turned the highway shoulder into an oven, the asphalt radiating heat that made the horizon shimmer like water. James and Nico made slow progress, their paws aching from the grit of the gravel. Every time a heavy cargo truck barreled past, the sheer force of the air pressure threatened to tip them over, forcing James to press himself low against the earth. The constant mechanical roar was overwhelming, a stark contrast to the quiet, ticking stillness of the Grand Library rafters he sometimes dreamed of when the trail grew too loud. Seeking refuge, he signaled to Nico, and they scrambled through a gap in the dense green stalks to find the deep, fragrant shade of the sugarcane field.

The respite was immediate. Inside the thicket, the air was cooler and smelled of damp earth and crushed greenery. As they picked their way through the maze of stalks, James spotted a wide, dark aperture at the base of the highway embankment: a concrete drainage culvert. It was a tunnel built to carry mountain runoff beneath the road, smelling of cool stone and shadow. With a quick check of his compass, James stepped into the mouth of the tunnel. The transition was sharp, the outside world's roar dulling into a distant, muffled hum as they padded through the damp concrete interior.

They emerged on the far side of the road, crawling out of the dark concrete tunnel into a quiet, shaded grove of cottonwood trees. Here, the highway was a distant memory, replaced by the soft rustle of silver-green leaves and the gentle trickle of a nearby irrigation ditch. It was the perfect sanctuary. They spent the remaining afternoon gathering soft, fallen leaves and dry twigs, weaving them together to create a protected sleeping nest beneath the gnarled roots of an ancient cottonwood.

As twilight deepened, James sat by their small, sheltered camp, watching the evening light filter through the cottonwood canopy. He took out his map to mark their crossing, feeling a quiet sense of triumph in having outsmarted the highway's noise. With the day's hard travel behind them, he shared a final piece of orange peel with Nico, the two travelers settling into the cool, silent embrace of the grove for the night.
location: A shaded cottonwood grove on the far side of the highway south of San Antonio del Río
